findings.requirement: A successfully acquired runtime must enter owned cleanup scope before subsequent prompt/MCP/task setup can fail.
findings.trigger: Classic interactive mode; composition.acquire succeeds; later prepare/prompt/MCP/bus setup fails before line 463 try.
findings.impact: Live/reused host can retain acquired resources until process exit or external cleanup; no permanent post-death lease/data-loss claim.
findings.counterevidence: One-shot path has immediate try/finally; process death releases OS locks; normal-flow test does not cover this failure chain.
findings.smallest_alternative: Enter owned try/finally immediately after acquire, retain incremental handles and reverse cleanup/terminal restoration.

findings.confidence: high mechanism; custom/concurrent failure incidence conditional
findings.requirement: Facade closure should fence new admission while preserving join/retry access to retained cleanup until release settles.
findings.trigger: Injected/custom composition close failure, concurrent close, BUILDING race or foreign-loop failure after facade sets _closed.
findings.impact: One boolean can make retained cleanup unreachable through facade or cause a concurrent close caller to return before release settles.
findings.counterevidence: Default no-channel acquisition may not suspend; normal SDK path has no cron/channel injection; ordinary close may succeed.
findings.smallest_alternative: Keep admission closed but retain a joinable close task/outcome and retry retained cleanup, or explicitly narrow public contract.

findings.requirement: Unsettled rollback ownership must remain reachable after partial acquisition failure.
findings.trigger: Injected factory starts resistant owned resource; later custom channel/cron acquisition fails; reverse cleanup hits RuntimeOwnedWorkError before earlier closers.
findings.impact: Local closer list can be lost when acquisition records FAILED without assigning _closers, preventing later retry of unresolved cleanup.
findings.counterevidence: No built-in constructor producing this resistant partial-build sequence established; ChannelManager has its own constructor rollback.
findings.smallest_alternative: Retain unresolved acquisition callbacks from first ownership, remove only settled closers, and use one recursive owned-error classifier.

findings.confidence: high mechanism; currently unreachable through guarded onboard entrypoint
findings.requirement: Config replacement should preserve prior complete bytes across crash/serialization/write failure.
findings.trigger: Legacy onboard gate is reactivated/bypassed and plugin defaults are written after initial atomic save.
findings.impact: Second open('w')/json.dump can truncate a previously valid config if the write fails; no current default corruption claim.
findings.counterevidence: require_runtime_ready currently always raises before onboard; canonical save_config is atomic.
findings.smallest_alternative: Merge defaults before one atomic save, or route the plugin-enriched JSON through the same atomic writer.

findings.requirement: Sensitive values should not be rendered raw or supplied as visible input defaults.
findings.trigger: Wizard entrypoint is reactivated/directly used with existing provider key lists or sensitive scalar edits.
findings.impact: Sensitive lists are joined raw; existing sensitive scalar can flow to text default; terminal capture may expose credentials.
findings.counterevidence: Main onboard is migration-gated; secret input helper exists; no real credential exposure observed.
findings.smallest_alternative: Propagate sensitivity recursively, use secret input with no secret default, and preserve explicit keep/cancel/back semantics including lists.

findings.confidence: high source mechanism; multi-config product contract unresolved
findings.requirement: An explicitly configured runtime should not silently consult mutable process-global config path/network policy for later effects unless one-config-per-process is the contract.
findings.trigger: SDK/custom config path or multiple config loads while generated media/network validators later consult global helpers.
findings.impact: Generated media can land under another/default media root and later config loads can alter process-global SSRF whitelist used by an earlier runtime.
findings.counterevidence: Normal CLI aligns global config path; no deployed multi-config incident or cross-user leak established.
findings.smallest_alternative: Pass captured media root/runtime network policy explicitly; alternatively define/enforce one-config-per-process while still aligning custom-path media.

findings.confidence: high mechanism; built-in false-ready producer mismatch narrowed
findings.requirement: Local gateway readiness checks should use one bounded proxy-independent parser/predicate and reject malformed/non-object payloads safely.
findings.trigger: Local health endpoint or proxy supplies valid non-object JSON, or compatibility endpoint returns status ok with ready false.
findings.impact: CLI/WebUI helper can raise AttributeError and proxy behavior differs; predicates disagree on ready=false.
findings.counterevidence: Built-in readiness producer emits status='degraded' when ready is false, so current built-in false-ready success is not established.
findings.smallest_alternative: Use one proxy-free bounded parser/predicate at management edge and delegate legacy helpers to it.

finding_count_convention: Seven distinct C00 entries; cross-module observations (GitStore, hard restart, compatibility stubs) remain tradeoffs/questions rather than extra findings.

final_discussion_questions.question: What executor/client platform promise should govern managed gateway, desktop/browser attachment and platform-specific process identity?
Should runtime media/network policy be captured per configured instance, or should one-config-per-process become an explicit enforced contract?
Do retained-task/delegation goals require any new startup/session framework here? Current C00 evidence does not justify one.
Which gated/public compatibility surfaces may be retired or reactivated: onboard wizard, model/evaluator stubs, Stage1 and desktop attach seams?
What MCP registration/cleanup/reload lifetime must composition expose, reconciled with H01/T01/E02?
What failure/retry contract should SDK close and explicit hard /restart provide?
What completion/quiescence guarantee is required versus bounded waits and retained ownership, including output/media/log/UI cleanup?
